value.rationale: A reset clock imposes an exploration-time cost even when the walker already occupies the search frontier. The natural optimal rate is globally classified for every step bias, revealing a sharp 3/4 drift transition and a quadratic small-benefit law. These are structurally informative for memory-directed exploration and search protocol design, not an arbitrary finite parameter selection. The basic geometric-gap method is elementary but the exact phase boundary addresses a motivated competition between reset benefits and frontier no-op costs.
